title: Use UUIDv7 for opaque, immutable node identifiers
context: Alternative approaches: sequential numbering (MOD-0042), path-derived naming, or globally unique GUIDs without time-ordering.
decision: Every node, edge, rule, decision, screen, flow, and registry entry carries a UUIDv7 as its `id`. The identifier is opaque, immutable, locally generated, and time-sortable. Every internal reference stores the `id` and nothing else.
consequences: No risk of collision from parallel agents minting MOD-0042 on different branches; local generation with no coordination needed; time-ordering available for sorting; UUIDs are opaque so humans must use slugs for readability.
